rationale.CT abdomen: Splenomegaly diagnosis is clinical. CT not indicated unless splenic rupture suspected.

hpi: {{patient_name}} is a 6-year-old child who presents with fever, sore throat, malaise, and generalized rash. Exam reveals posterior cervical lymphadenopathy, palatal petechiae, and splenomegaly. The combination of pharyngitis, lymphadenopathy, fever, and the characteristic maculopapular rash is classic for infectious mononucleosis caused by Epstein-Barr virus. The differential includes other viral infections (CMV, acute HIV), streptococcal pharyngitis, and toxoplasmosis. Key management considerations: avoid amoxicillin/ampicillin (causes characteristic EBV rash), avoid aspirin (Reye syndrome risk in febrile children), and in older patients, restrict contact sports to prevent splenic rupture.

physical_exam: Febrile, lethargic child. Sore throat, malaise.
Splenomegaly — classic finding in mononucleosis. Palpable spleen tip.
Maculopapular rash — characteristic of EBV infection.
Posterior cervical lymphadenopathy. Palatal petechiae. Pharyngeal erythema with tonsillar exudates.

case_summary: Classic pediatric mononucleosis. Fever + pharyngitis + lymphadenopathy + splenomegaly. Monospot/EBV serology confirms. Symptomatic treatment: acetaminophen, rest. Avoid aspirin (Reye's) and amoxicillin/ampicillin (drug rash). Office management.
